title.value: Mitigating Calibration Bias Without Fixed Attribute Grouping for Improved Fairness in Medical Imaging Analysis
title.justification: The title encapsulates the paper's primary focus on reducing calibration bias in medical imaging analysis without relying on predetermined attribute groupings.
title.quote: Title of the paper: Mitigating Calibration Bias Without Fixed Attribute Grouping for Improved Fairness in Medical Imaging Analysis

extractions.description: This paper proposes a two-stage method called "Cluster-Focal" to address calibration biases in medical imaging. The method identifies poorly calibrated samples and clusters them to optimize bias reduction using group-wise focal loss. It is evaluated on two medical imaging tasks related to skin lesion classification and predicting lesional activity in multiple sclerosis patients. The method shows improvement in controlling calibration error without significant loss in prediction performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on calibration bias in medical imaging rather than directly relating to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Trustworthy deployment of deep learning medical imaging models into real-world clinical practice requires that they be calibrated. However, models that are well calibrated overall can still be poorly calibrated for a sub-population, potentially resulting in a clinician unwittingly making poor decisions for this group based on the recommendations of the model.

primary_category.quote: Our method does not require subgroup attributes during training, permitting the flexibility to mitigate biases for different choices of sensitive attributes without re-training.

secondary_categories.quote: Deep learning models have shown high prediction performance on many medical imaging tasks.

applications.quote: Our results demonstrate that our method effectively controls calibration error in the worst-performing subgroups while preserving prediction performance, and outperforming recent baselines.
